method: Black-box process input/output measurements plus primary hardware documentation; no GPL bus implementation source consulted for this measurement.

oracle.accessTiming: completed-tick-boundary; reads/writes consume no implicit cycles
oracle.stdout: PCM generated by the oracle was discarded; no PCM or music content is stored in this report.

replay: For an exact batch replay, emit the oracle header for its model, then concatenate commands for the listed probeIds in order. Array commands are joined with spaces and reset strings are literal protocol lines. One oracle instance serves each batch. Reset clears its bus but does not imply that all oscillator/envelope initial conditions are recreated.
searchMethod: Fresh processes: w0=165; cN; r31. Double N from1 until the first zero bracket, then binary-search last retained / first zero. The boundary witnesses are repeated below.

primaryHardwareSources.title: MOS6581 datasheet (original document reproduced by Simon Inns)
facts: POT conversion updates every512 PHI2 cycles and depends on external resistance/capacitance.
Unused offsets29..31 do not store writes and return unspecified data.
Bus access requires CS asserted, PHI2 high and the appropriate R/W level.
primaryHardwareSources.limits: The datasheet does not specify a fixed write-only bus retention lifetime or a halve-on-read rule.

primaryHardwareSources.title: SID die reverse engineering: Data Bus
facts: Input write drives the internal bus even for read-only or nonexistent registers.
A read-only register drives its current value onto the internal bus.
Write-only and nonexistent reads expose the previous valid internal bus value.
Undriven bus value fades depending on chip model and temperature.
primaryHardwareSources.limits: Primary circuit analysis, not emulator implementation. It does not establish the fixed thresholds measured from this oracle.

primaryHardwareSources.title: SID die reverse engineering: Registers
facts: OSC3 exposes upper8 waveform bits through a latch and the internal bus.

primaryHardwareSources.title: SID die reverse engineering: POT registers
facts: POT latches drive the internal data bus; their analog conversion is separate from the SID waveform generator.

summaries.byteDecayObservation: All tested bits disappear together at the same observed threshold; no per-bit fade pattern exposed by this oracle.
summaries.normalWriteOnlyReadObservation: For measured waits leaving positive post-read life, the observed expiry matches floor(previous remaining cycles/2), without refreshing the byte.
summaries.zeroResidualAnomaly: When the normal shortening pattern predicts zero residual, a nonzero byte can remain visible after subsequent clocks, including twice the fresh-write threshold. This is an observed reference anomaly, not a measured internal timer or physical SID guarantee.
summaries.readableObservation: OSC3/ENV3 current output and reference default POT255 replace the previous latch value and refill the whole model lifetime; a zero-readable value clears the old nonzero bus.
summaries.resetObservation: Initial write-only reads and explicit reset return a zero bus in this oracle.

selectedResearchWrapperPolicy.status: Chosen approximation for the isolated prototype; not proof of physical hardware and not production Player adoption.
selectedResearchWrapperPolicy.validWrites: Every register offset0..31 loads the written byte and refills its model lifetime, including read-only and unused register addresses.
selectedResearchWrapperPolicy.oscillatorEnvelopeReads: OSC3/ENV3 load each candidate own current readback and refill its model lifetime. Do not substitute oracle data.
selectedResearchWrapperPolicy.writeOnlyReads: Return the retained byte; for a nonzero byte with positive remaining lifetime, shorten to max(1,floor(remaining/2)). Clocking the final remaining cycle clears the latch.
selectedResearchWrapperPolicy.deliberateDivergence: When the oracle shortens residual1 to0 it can retain a nonzero byte after2T cycles. The bounded prototype instead leaves1cycle and clears it on the next tick.
selectedResearchWrapperPolicy.potReads: POTX/POTY are explicitly unsupported in the isolated candidate and must fail without changing bus, register or cycle state; oracle default255 is recorded only as a diagnostic.
selectedResearchWrapperPolicy.clocks: Reads/writes add no implicit clocks. Only explicit clock/tick advances age the latch.
selectedResearchWrapperPolicy.resetStop: Clear the isolated bus on reset/Stop.

recommendedInterpretation: Fixed per-model thresholds and read shortening are reference-matching approximations, not universal hardware constants.
Do not reproduce the zero-residual immortal-latch anomaly as a physical hardware claim; choose and document an explicitly bounded approximation.
POT=255 here is an external-reference default without supplied analog input. The isolated candidate may reject POT rather than invent a conversion or silent constant.
Bus latch is distinct from written-register shadow. Writes to read-only/unused offsets load the bus but do not change that readable hardware state.
OSC3/ENV3 must use each candidate own state and drive that value into the bus and the CPU; no reference readback substitution or writes-only replay.
limits: Only a pinned external emulator was measured, not physical SID silicon or temperature/voltage variants.
Probe accesses are at completed-clock boundaries; this does not measure within-PHI2 analog timing.
Only48kHz output was requested; bus tests are measured in chip cycles independently of emitted PCM.
